# Data and code

We publish every reform, year, and trust-fund split on the
[interactive dashboard](https://policyengine.org/us/taxation-of-benefits-reforms).
Its
[results file](https://policyengine.org/us/taxation-of-benefits-reforms/data/results.csv)
holds every static and labor-supply row, with a column that labels each row an
exact anchor or an interpolation. Each of the 323 exact rows names its run, the
SHA-256 hash of its reform H5 file, and where we store that file and its
metadata. We also publish a
[file that traces each row to its inputs](https://policyengine.org/us/taxation-of-benefits-reforms/data/results_contract.json),
with the hash of each exact row's baseline H5, each interpolated row's anchor
years, the base dataset, the baseline manifests, and the calibration targets with
their sources.

We built the baselines at commits `3de8abb6` and `c5e4f1a6` of the
[crfb-tob-impacts repository](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/crfb-tob-impacts)
and produced the exact rows in ten runs, all on `policyengine-us` 1.700.2,
`policyengine.py` 4.5.1, and `policyengine-core` 3.26.1. The two labor-supply
runs also apply the
[`Simulation.delete_arrays` change](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/crfb-tob-impacts/blob/main/docs/current/patches/policyengine-core-3.26.1-delete-arrays.patch)
from `policyengine-core` 3.30.1, which the substitution response needs. Their
metadata records the base package version and not that change. A script reads
the metadata file of every exact row and writes each run's Python and package
versions, reforms, and years, and each baseline's calibration, weight, and
contributor figures, to
[`docs/current/run-provenance.json`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/crfb-tob-impacts/blob/main/docs/current/run-provenance.json).

The
[crfb-tob-impacts repository](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/crfb-tob-impacts)
holds the code that projects the microdata, scores the reforms, and builds the
results tables. There, `scripts/build_headline_summary.py` computes the headline
summary from the results file and the Trustees' effective interest rates, and
`scripts/generate_paper_static_exhibits.py` writes the other results tables from
the same file. The repository's tests fail if the committed tables differ from
what these scripts produce.
